decisions.statement: A path is named behind `--file-path` as `write` and `remove` name a path.
A path with no flag before the path is refused rather than read as a named path.
Nothing but `--file-path` names a path.
No folder is taken.
No whole tree is taken.
No flag meaning a folder or a whole tree is taken.
A path HEAD has no file at and the git index has no entry for is refused.
A path HEAD has no file at and the working tree holds a file at is refused.
A path only the git index holds, as a file, has that git index entry cleared.
A path only the git index holds as anything but a file is refused.
A file this command is named is never deleted from the working tree.
A path HEAD holds as anything but a file is refused.
One path refused refuses the whole call.
The body written is the body HEAD has byte for byte.
The git index is written to the mode and the object HEAD holds.
A path whose working tree and git index both have HEAD's body is left alone and said so.
A path whose git index alone has another body is put back too.
A git index entry cleared is said as its own case rather than as a restore.
No working tree file is written where a git index entry alone is cleared.
The body each path discards is said before the body each path was put back to.
Nothing is committed.
No check runs.
No warrant is owed.
No reading is forgotten.
Uncommitted drift goes without a git call that could take another agent's work.
A restore git broke or stopped part way is refused as the machine's fault.
That refusal names each path put back before it stopped, not the report alone.
A path HEAD names and holds no body for is refused as the data's fault.
Every other refusal here is the caller's fault.
A call refused more than once is answered by the worst of those faults.
`--file-path` is named again for each path put back.

definition: the command putting named paths back to what HEAD says, in the working tree and the git index
